{
  "problem": "Design a minimal REST API for managing tasks, including endpoint definitions and JSON data structures.",
  "objectives": [
    "Define standard RESTful CRUD endpoints for task management.",
    "Design the JSON schema for task entities and API responses."
  ],
  "deliverables": [
    "OpenAPI 3.0 specification document defining endpoints, methods, and schemas.",
    "JSON schema definitions for Task entity, Create/Update requests, and standard error responses.",
    "List of RESTful endpoints (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) with expected HTTP status codes."
  ],
  "constraints": [
    "The API design must remain minimal with no extraneous endpoints.",
    "The architecture must strictly follow REST principles and standard HTTP methods.",
    "The data exchange format must be exclusively JSON.",
    "The final response must be structured as a valid JSON object."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "Task entity includes core attributes: id (UUID), title (string), description (string), status (enum: pending, in_progress, completed), created_at (ISO 8601), and due_date (ISO 8601).",
    "The API defines a standard error response structure containing HTTP status code, error type, and descriptive message.",
    "The deliverable is a pure API design document (JSON/OpenAPI schema) without specific backend framework implementation code.",
    "PATCH is used for partial updates and PUT for full replacements."
  ],
  "non_goals": [
    "Implementing user authentication, API keys, or authorization mechanisms.",
    "Implementing advanced filtering, sorting, or pagination parameters.",
    "Providing backend database schemas (SQL DDL or NoSQL document structures).",
    "Writing backend routing or controller code in specific programming languages or frameworks."
  ],
  "acceptance": [
    "All CRUD operations for tasks are mapped to standard HTTP methods and hierarchical URIs.",
    "JSON schemas for task creation, task update, and task retrieval are fully defined with explicit data types and required fields.",
    "Standard HTTP status codes (200, 201, 204, 400, 404, 422, 500) are correctly assigned to all endpoint responses.",
    "The final output is delivered as a syntactically valid JSON structure."
  ],
  "risks": [
    "Over-engineering the minimal API by adding unnecessary nested resources or complex query parameters.",
    "Ambiguity in partial updates if the distinction between PUT and PATCH is not explicitly defined in the schema.",
    "Omitting pagination in the initial design may require breaking changes to the GET collection endpoint when scaling."
  ]
}
